Elena — attaching the canonical roster (redwood_subprocessors_2027-04.csv) and a zip with supporting artifacts (redwood_supplychain_evidence_v1.zip). Quick answers inline below; see attachments for mapping and evidence stamps.

- Canonical roster: included in CSV (vendor, primary function, country, onshore/offshore flag). Top entries: AWS (us-east-1, cloud infra, US), Google Cloud (europe-west4, cloud infra, EU), HashiCorp Vault (secrets mgmt, US), PostgreSQL managed (database-as-a-service, US/EU), Datadog (monitoring, US), Sentry (error monitoring, US), Segment (event routing, US) and a few specialized inference partners (inference-ops, EU/US).

- Access to raw prompts/embeddings: For hosted API, raw prompts and generated outputs are processed in-memory on the inference runtime; persistent storage of raw prompts is not performed as a matter of course. Exceptions: customers who opt into "debug/retention" for troubleshooting may have short-term snapshots (retention configurable, default 7 days). The only subprocessors that might see raw content in those debug flows are our debug log storage provider and a secure, access-controlled archive (both noted in CSV). For Dedicated/Private (VPC/on-prem), customers can opt for customer-managed keys and turn off retention — in that configuration Redwood does not retain raw content.

- KMS ownership: Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default (we maintain key lifecycle in our KMS). We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS) for Dedicated and Private customers. KMS ownership is captured per-account in our onboarding doc; see attachment "kms-ownership-matrix.pdf" inside the zip.

- KV cache & persistence: Runtime KV cache is ephemeral and lives on GPU RAM or ephemeral instance storage; it is not written to long-term object storage. Telemetry/logging may contain hashed identifiers and non-sensitive metadata; raw content is excluded except for the debug snapshot flow noted above. Retention windows for telemetry/logs: default 30 days (configurable up to 90 for enterprise customers).

- APAC subprocessors / PHI handling: We have APAC-based infra partners for edge routing in Singapore and Sydney (listed in the CSV). For workloads with PHI restrictions, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with CMK and region pinning. We will flag any APAC subprocessors that have had PHI access and provide attestation.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2027-04.csv (canonical roster), redwood_supplychain_evidence_v1.zip (contains SOC2 cover letter, KMS matrix, sample audit logs).

If you want, we can provide a redacted CAIQ and SIG-lite next.

--Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

3) Can you confirm which subprocessors are located in APAC and whether any of those subprocessors operate as sub-subprocessors (i.e., do you rely on a vendor who in turn uses another vendor in APAC)?

Procurement note: our legal team will need the SOC2 report and a signed attestation about data residency for PHI workloads.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Third-party supply chain / subprocessor roster and clarifications

Elena — quick follow-up with concrete controls: 

- Debug snapshots: access is tightly controlled. Only members of our Security Engineering team (a small on-call group) can request snapshot access via the internal ticketing system. Approvals require two approvers (Security lead + Eng manager), enforced by the ticketing workflow; access tokens are time-limited (max 48 hours) and all access is logged and audited. We require MFA and single-use escalation for retrieval of any snapshot.

- Hashed identifiers: we use salted hashing with per-customer salts for any telemetry identifiers. There is no reversible mapping stored in the telemetry pipeline; reversibility would require the salt and an internal mapping which we do not persist for telemetry. For customer-managed retention/debug flows, customers may opt into storage that includes reversible artifacts for their own troubleshooting — that is explicitly documented and opt-in.

- APAC subprocessors: the CSV marks APAC vendors (Singapore: edge-router-sg, Sydney: edge-router-syd). A small subset of our log aggregation partner uses regional aggregation partners in APAC; we have contractual flow-downs and attestations with those sub-subprocessors (attestations included in the zip). We will flag any sub-subprocessor contact details and provide their control matrices.

- SOC2 / attestation: Monica included the SOC2 cover letter in the zip. We can provide the full SOC2 report under an NDA/secure link. For PHI workloads: we will provide a signed attestation that for Dedicated/Private deployments (with CMK and region pinning) Redwood will not export content outside customer-controlled regions. We can draft the attestation and route via DocuSign if that helps procurement.

Action items:
- Monica: prepare redacted CAIQ & SIG-lite and include attestation language for PHI residency (target 2027-04-06).
- Marissa: will coordinate the secure transfer of SOC2 (NDA or secure link).

-Karthik
Vendor Risk, Redwood Inference
